title: B41 · Paid is not done, and delivered is not done either
anchor: Build 24, the paid job that stayed open; the delivery loop follow up drafted 9 September 2026

slides.headline: PAID IS NOT DONE. DELIVERED IS NOT DONE EITHER.
slides.sub: The box arrived on time and I still had no idea whether the client was happy.
slides.boundary: No client, job or order in this document is a real one.

slides.h2: A JOB THAT WAS FINISHED, DELIVERED AND PAID
lede: It sat open on our board for weeks. Nobody forgot on purpose. There was simply no moment in anybody's day that said this one is over now.
The money had landed. The board still showed it as work.
slides.boundary: Which means every number read off that board was wrong for weeks.

slides.h2: WHERE JOBS GO TO DIE QUIETLY

left.p: Accounting is satisfied, the board is not updated, and the rep has moved on to the next fire.

right.p: The tracking says delivered. Nobody has asked a human being whether the thing was right.

slides.boundary: Two different endings, both of them treated as the same word.

items.text: Delivery lands and the job stops asking for attention
A week later the system drafts one short message
I read it, change a word, and press send
The answer gets filed against the job, not my inbox
Only then does the job read as closed

slides.boundary: Four of the five steps ask nothing of anybody. Step three is the whole job.

slides.eyebrow: WHAT THE HUMAN HAS TO DO
slides.label: press of send, on a message that is already written and already knows which job it is about.
slides.sub: Every field this loop needs is a field a machine already fills. That is the only reason it will still be running in six months.
slides.boundary: A follow up that needs somebody to remember is a follow up that stops in week three.

slides.quote: If a step in your process depends on somebody feeling like it, that step does not exist. Write it down as not existing.
slides.src: Measured version: every field a human must type here sits between 0 and 15 percent filled.
slides.boundary: The loop was built to survive a bad week, not a good one.

slides.h2: YOU CAN RUN THIS WITHOUT SOFTWARE
lede: Pick your last twenty delivered jobs. Count how many of them you actually know the outcome of. Not the tracking status, the outcome.
Then ask what would have had to happen for you to know. In most shops it is one message, a week late, that nobody owns.
slides.boundary: The gap is never the sending. It is the remembering.

slides.h2: SEE THE LOOP ON YOUR OWN JOBS
lede: Access is by request rather than a signup button, and I will show it against your own channels.
